children: Emeco's FY 2027 guidance is slightly below BMO Capital Markets's expectations. Emeco expects annual operating Ebitda of A$275 million-A$285 million. The mining equipment provider also expects a skew toward 2H. Analyst Gavin Allen had forecast Ebitda of A$289.5 million ahead of Emeco's update. Still, BMO sees FY 2028 as a more important year for earnings. Emeco expects utilization at end-FY 2027 to deliver FY 2028 earnings growth consistent with its target for a 20% return on capital. Key drivers for this are higher fleet utilization and operating leverage. "Achieving these targets translates to solid earnings and cash flow generation increases over the medium term," says BMO, which rated Emeco at outperform ahead of today's update. Emeco is down 8.1% at A$1.14. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
